angle: How reusable nappies pay for themselves within 7 months of full-time use
count_rationale: 10 cards chosen to support the numeric break-even narrative. The topic warrants multiple cost-comparison cards (big_number + split) plus exploration of the three practical approaches (categories). This density is justified by the research depth and the target audience's need for concrete financial reassurance.

cards.headline: 8,000 nappies. One decision. Break-even in 7 months.
cards.key_message: Lead with the concrete number (8,000 nappies) and the payoff promise (break-even) to create curiosity and quantified expectation.
cards.content_note: From research: 'Each child uses approximately 6–8 nappies per day, totalling 8,000 nappies from birth to toilet training' + 'Break-even timeline is approximately 7 months of full-time cloth nappy use'. This is the hook statement from the research.
cards.layout_hint: Large single number (8,000) above headline. Dark/rich background for contrast.

cards.headline: You're spending $2,500+ on nappies by toilet training. Want to cut that in half?
cards.subheading_hint: 화장실 훈련까지 다이퍼에 $2,500 이상을 쓰고 있어요. 그걸 절반으로 줄이고 싶나요?
cards.key_message: Yes-question that immediately signals the financial pain point and the relief cloth nappies offer. Speaks to the audience's budget consciousness.
cards.content_note: From research: 'Disposable nappies cost $2,500–$4,000 per child over 2.5–3 years until toilet training' vs 'Cloth nappies cost $720–$910 for a full stash plus washing costs ($150–$200 per year), totalling under $1,000'.
cards.layout_hint: Conversational tone. Use a question mark. Light background for readability.

cards.headline: Disposable: $2,500–$4,000. Cloth: Under $1,000 total.
cards.key_message: Stark cost comparison drives home the financial advantage of cloth. The gap is immediate and undeniable.
cards.content_note: From research: 'Disposable nappies cost $2,500–$4,000 per child over 2.5–3 years' + 'Cloth nappies cost $720–$910 for a full stash (24 nappies) plus washing costs ($150–$200 per year), totalling under $1,000 for the entire nappy-wearing period.' This includes both upfront stash + all washing costs over the full period.
cards.layout_hint: Two columns or side-by-side: left side ($2,500–$4,000 in red or darker shade), right side ($1,000 in green or lighter shade) to emphasize the savings.

cards.headline: Modern cloth nappies aren't your parents' cloth nappies.
cards.subheading_hint: 현대식 천 다이퍼는 부모 세대의 것과 다릅니다.
cards.key_message: Bold, empowering truth that directly addresses the common misconception in the research. Shifts the narrative from 'hassle' to 'innovation'.
cards.content_note: From research common_misconception: 'Cloth nappies smell bad and are labour-intensive to maintain.' Counter: modern MCNs have built-in waterproofing, adjustable snaps, and designs that fit as easily as disposables. This card breaks rhythm and adds emotional reassurance.
cards.layout_hint: Dark card background. Single bold headline. No body copy. Add subtle visual of a modern snap/waterproof element if possible.

cards.headline: Cost per nappy: $0.50 (disposable) vs $0.09 (cloth).
cards.key_message: Per-unit cost comparison reinforces the numeric advantage. Shows that cloth is cheaper on every single change, not just over time.
cards.content_note: From research: 'Disposable nappies cost $0.25–$0.88 per nappy (average $0.50); cloth nappies, when amortised across 8,000 nappies, cost around $0.09 per nappy after the first year.' This is the amortized cost after break-even.
cards.layout_hint: Two boxes or circles with large numbers. Emphasize the 5x difference visually. Use calculation notation ($0.50 ÷ $0.09 = 5.5x).

cards.headline: Break-even = the month when cloth saves equal your upfront cost.
cards.subheading_hint: 손익분기점 = 천 다이퍼 절약액이 초기 비용과 같아지는 달.
cards.key_message: Define 'break-even' in plain language so readers understand the milestone and its importance. Sets up the 7-month payoff.
cards.content_note: From research definition: 'Break-even is the point at which your upfront cloth nappy investment ($400–$1,000) equals the amount you would have spent on disposables in the same timeframe. For Australian families, this occurs around 7 months of daily use. After break-even, cloth nappies continue saving money for every subsequent month until toilet training.'
cards.layout_hint: Simple diagram or timeline showing month 0 (upfront cost) → month 7 (break-even) → month 30+ (continuous savings). Use a visual timeline.

cards.headline: Three ways to go cloth (pick what fits your life).
cards.subheading_hint: 천 다이퍼를 사용하는 세 가지 방법 (당신의 생활에 맞는 것을 선택하세요).
cards.key_message: Acknowledge that cloth isn't one-size-fits-all. Present realistic options so families feel ownership over their choice.
cards.content_note: From research contrasting_approaches: (1) 'Full-time cloth (24-nappy stash)' — max savings ($2,000+) by month 7; (2) 'Hybrid or part-time (8–12 nappies)' — moderate savings (~$1,000 over 2.5 years) with less commitment; (3) 'Overnight disposable boost' — cloth full-time day, disposables overnight.
cards.layout_hint: Three boxes or cards stacked vertically or in a row. Label each with approach name, upfront cost range, and annual savings. Use checkmarks or badges for pros.

cards.headline: Do: Start with a trial stash of 8–12. Don't: Buy 24 nappies and panic.
cards.subheading_hint: 할 것: 8–12개의 시험 묶음으로 시작하세요. 하지 말 것: 24개를 사서 불안해하지 마세요.
cards.key_message: Reduce buyer's remorse and decision paralysis by giving permission to start small. Also address detergent/washing myths that create resistance.
cards.content_note: From research do_examples: 'Start with a trial stash of 10 nappies at home on weekends to prove to yourself that modern cloth nappies are as easy as disposables.' Also from dont_examples: 'Don't use too much detergent, which causes ammonia smells' + 'Don't commit to 24 nappies immediately if you're unsure. Start with 8–12 for part-time use.'
cards.layout_hint: Two-column layout. Left side (green/positive): 'Do' advice. Right side (amber/cautionary): 'Don't' advice. Use icons or checkmarks vs X marks.

cards.headline: Cloth Nappy Break-Even Cheat Sheet
cards.key_message: Screenshot-friendly reference card with all key numbers and timelines for quick recall and sharing.
cards.content_note: Synthesize: upfront costs ($400–$1,000), break-even timeline (7 months), annual savings after break-even ($400–$600), cost per nappy ($0.50 disposable vs $0.09 cloth), council rebates (up to $200), nappy count per day (6–8), total nappies needed (8,000), reuse savings (2nd child $400 + washing only).
cards.layout_hint: Table format with rows: 'Upfront cost', 'Break-even month', 'Nappies per day', 'Annual savings (after month 7)', 'Cost per nappy', 'Council rebate available', 'Reuse savings (child 2)'. Include footnote: 'Australian prices and availability vary by state/council.'
cards.content_structure: Use small/compact font to fit all data. Rows should be scannable. Include a QR code or link to council rebate checker if space allows.

cards.headline: Ready to save $2,000? Save this carousel + share with a parent who's drowning in nappy costs.
cards.subheading_hint: $2,000를 절약할 준비가 되셨나요? 이 카로셀을 저장하고 다이퍼 비용에 허덕이는 부모님과 공유하세요.
cards.key_message: Action prompt that speaks to nappyprice's audience: savers who want to share wins with others. Use specific emotion ('drowning') and specific action ('save + share').
cards.content_note: Standard CTA with brand voice: concrete action (save), peer-to-peer sharing (share with another parent), and emotional resonance (drowning in costs).
cards.layout_hint: Centered text with clear button/action zones for 'Save' and 'Share'. Include comment prompt: 'Tell us in the comments: Are you cloth or disposable? What's your break-even looking like?'
